description: An ordinary web link reopens at its own URL with no earlier page history; a forwarded port keeps its reload semantics. Needs a local HTTP server and a device, so the runner only launches the chat; the scenes below are driven by hand.
automatedCoverage: None: launching the chat proves nothing about page history, cookies or request counts. JVM coverage is ChatWebViewPoolTest and ChatLinkReopenTest, which use Robolectric shadows and do not run a real renderer.

localServer.description: Serve from the host machine and reach it from the device over a non-loopback address (adb reverse would make it a loopback port link). Count every request per path.

pages./a: Page A with a link to /b and a visible request counter
pages./b: Page B with a link back to /a
pages./login: Sets a long-lived cookie named session and redirects to /a
pages./whoami: Echoes whether the session cookie arrived

steps: Send a message containing the /a link and tap it
Tap the link to /b inside the page
Close the card, then tap the same message link again
Repeat the close and reopen three times
manualScenes.expect: Every reopen shows /a with the card's Back going straight to close (no page history). The server sees one /a request per opening and no request to /b after the first visit. No second renderer piles up: the process lists at most four WebView renderers.

steps: Receive an Agent reply containing the /a link and wait for the list to stop scrolling
manualScenes.expect: The page is already loaded when the card rises. The server saw the /a request before the tap, not after.

steps: Close, reopen /whoami, and watch the server log
manualScenes.expect: /whoami reports the cookie after every reopen: a new renderer shares the cookie store. The log shows no cache or cookie wipe side effects (a cached sub-resource is not fetched again).

steps: Open /a, go to /b, shrink the card to Peek and expand it again
Select text on a page and use AI edit, then Use as context
manualScenes.expect: Peek does not reload the page. The first Back returns to /a, the second closes the card. The selection actions carry the same context content as before.

steps: Run a dev server on the computer and tap its localhost link in an Agent reply
Change a served file, close the card and tap the link again
With the card open, edit a file that triggers hot reload
Stop the server and tap the link
manualScenes.expect: The reopened port shows the new content. Hot reload keeps working while the card is open. The phone's own loopback receives no request before the tap. A stopped server reports the 404 notice as before.

steps: Open a Feishu document link with the Lark extension on: the native reader shows, no page is loaded
Choose Open as web page, close and reopen
Kill the page's renderer process from adb on a web link and tap Reload
manualScenes.expect: The reader shows without a WebView until switched; after the switch a closed page reopens fresh. A killed renderer shows the quit notice and Reload builds a new view. Not verifiable on a device if the renderer cannot be killed safely: report it as not verified on device.
